Looking at each option for humor:

(A) "the sudm of all fears" - Just a random typo, not humorous

(B) "the mum of all fears" - Changes "sum" to "mum" (British/Australian slang for mother). This is humorous because "the mother of all [X]" is a well-known idiom meaning something is the greatest/most extreme example of that thing. The wordplay creates a clever double meaning.

(C) "the sums of all fears" - Just a grammatical change to plural, not humorous

(D) "the sum of all fear" - Just a grammatical change to singular, not humorous

The answer is clearly **(B)** because it creates a genuine pun/wordplay by substituting "sum" with "mum" to create the recognized idiom "the mother of all fears."

ANSWER: (B)
